records.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
records.response_pred: I know this is tough, but we've been through worse. Let's sit down and talk it through, okay? We'll figure this out together.

records.response_truth: No, you haven't. But you kept us alive and organised when the rest of us were too overwhelmed to think straight, so it evens out. I think we all showed up in the ways we were capable of. That's probably the best you can ask for.
records.response_pred: I've noticed. We all have our rough patches. What's been going on?

records.response_truth:
I know. And I'm not going to pretend I'm not annoyed about it, because I am — we had a rationing plan and you wrote it. But I also know that if things had got really bad, you'd have used it for all of us, not just yourself. At least I think that's true.

Is that what you're telling me? That it was for all of us?
records.response_pred: Sure, but let's make sure it's actually an emergency before we use it. We don't want to deplete our supplies unnecessarily.

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
records.response_truth:
Honestly? I would have called out the food and drink situation earlier instead of waiting and letting it sit. I knew something was off and I kept thinking about the right moment to bring it up and there probably wasn't ever going to be a perfect moment — I should have just said it directly when I first saw the bottle.

I think I also spent a lot of energy managing how everyone was feeling at the expense of saying what I actually thought. Which isn't always wrong, but there were times I softened things that probably didn't need softening.

What about you? What's your answer to your own question?
records.response_pred: If I had to do it over, I wouldn't have been so cautious about moving around. We missed a couple of opportunities to scout further, but staying put kept us safe. I guess I just err on the side of caution, you know? Writing that up will be good to reflect on it all.

records.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
records.response_truth:
That's probably a good idea actually. Might be useful for other people in the same situation — like, what actually works when you're rationing with almost nothing, what the real priorities are versus what you think they'll be. The water source being two hours away on foot, the mirror panel, all of it. Someone could genuinely benefit from that.

Send it to me when it's done. I mean that.
records.response_pred: Alright, I'll help with that. Let's gather everything tonight before we hit the hay. It'll be a good way to wind down after such a busy week.

records.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
records.response_truth:
None, really. They didn't serve a practical purpose. That was kind of the point.

I think when everything is stripped back to just survival — water, food, signal, shelter — and someone still makes room to draw flowers next to an SOS sign, that's them refusing to stop being a person. It's easy to become purely functional when the stakes are that high. DaVinci didn't.

I didn't fully appreciate it at the time either, if I'm honest. But I do now.
records.response_pred: They were probably just for fun, to brighten up our days and remind us of home, ya know? Maybe he was practicing his skills. But if you want, we can go look at them again tomorrow and try to figure it out. Might help us remember why we’re out here.
